steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: NEA Task 1 is a food investigation worth 15% of the total GCSE grade (AQA 8585). It is completed in controlled conditions over approximately 10 hours.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The investigation assesses students' understanding of the working characteristics, functional properties, and chemical processes of ingredients.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Task 1 involves: researching the given brief, conducting practical experiments, recording results, and writing a scientific report (1,500–2,000 words plus supporting evidence).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A typical Task 1 brief might ask you to investigate how different raising agents affect the volume and texture of a sponge cake, or how different fats affect pastry shortness.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Structure your investigation report clearly: Introduction, Research, Hypothesis, Method, Results, Analysis, Conclusion. Always name your variables: independent (what you change), dependent (what you measure), controlled (what you keep the same). Use food science terminology in your analysis: say 'denaturation of proteins' not 'the egg went hard', 'gelatinisation of starch' not 'the sauce thickened'. Photograph every stage of your investigation — visual evidence is essential supporting evidence.
